Name: many_shot_averages_detours
Title: Reading the Whole Bank Averages Out Detours: Many-Shot Context Is Robust to Per-Item Noise Where Top-k Retrieval Commits to It
Short Hypothesis: When the bank holds the agent's own successful-but-detoured trajectories (self pool) instead of expert trajectories, top-k retrieval passes the detours of the items it commits to (the rank-1 item above all) into the episode (more steps, more step-limit failures, lower success), while the whole-bank route is insensitive to the detour rate because the shared procedure is the consensus across many noisy items and idiosyncratic detours have no consensus; the gap between routes grows with the bank's detour rate and with item count, and closes when detours (not merely tokens) are pruned from the items.
Related Work: Bertsch et al. (arxiv:2405.00200) report that long-context ICL gains come from attention to the most similar examples rather than cumulative learning, and arxiv:2412.16926 that long-context models are less sensitive to example selection; both predict that a whole-bank prompt inherits whatever its most similar item contains, the opposite of consensus reading. In-context learning with noisy labels (arxiv:2411.19581) and many-shot ICL (arxiv:2404.11018, including Unsupervised and Reinforced ICL with model-generated examples) study label noise in classification, not action noise in trajectories. ExpeL and SkillEvolBench (arxiv:2605.24117) reuse raw on-policy trajectories and report episode-specific drift and clutter from larger libraries without stating how items were selected; Honest Lying (arxiv:2605.29463) shows reflexive agents storing confident wrong interpretations; MemoryGraft (arxiv:2512.16962) and the compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) show agents imitating implanted or conflicting retrieved experiences. None sets the detour rate of a trajectory bank at several levels and compares whole-bank reading with top-k retrieval on task success and steps.
Abstract: Long-context in-context learning studies report that gains from many demonstrations come from attention to the most similar examples rather than from cumulative learning, which predicts that reading a whole bank of trajectories inherits whatever the most similar item contains. We test the opposite on agent trajectories, where per-item noise has a natural form: the detours in the agent's own successful episodes. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B we build banks from the expert pool (no detours), the self pool (every item detoured), a high-detour self pool matched to the self pool on type and expert solution length, a pruned self pool whose detour visits are removed by rule and re-validated by replay, and a sham-pruned pool built from the same items with the same number of tokens removed elsewhere and every detour kept. Each bank is read by goal-sentence top-3 retrieval or whole in a cached prefix at 6, 24 and 48 items, on the same 274 games and two seeds; the four route x pool cells that decide the headline (retrieval and whole-bank, expert and self) are extended to four or six seeds by a pre-registered rule, blind to the effect's sign, until the interaction's minimum detectable effect is below 9 net. Whole-bank prefixes are drawn per game block and seed so that the most-similar item's detour and the bank-mean detour vary within an arm. Two composition arms put a self item at rank 1 only, or at ranks 2-3 only, of an otherwise expert triple. We score success, steps and step-limit failures against the Measurement C static arms and a self-pool static3. We predict that retrieval passes detours into the episode through the rank-1 item, that the whole-bank route is insensitive to the detour rate on success and on steps and improves with item count on the self pool only, that pruning restores retrieval where the sham-prune does not, and that whole-bank episodes do not track the most-similar item's detours within a pre-registered slope bound. Costs under caching are measured, since the robust route is also the longer prefix.
Experiments:
- Pools and banks. E: expert pool (1,465). S: self pool (1,892 successes). Per item: detour steps = steps beyond the expert solution length for the same game; detour visits = receptacle visits that did not yield the target object plus repeated identical actions; reported by stratum (type x expert-solution-length tercile). A: within each stratum the top tercile of S by detour steps, stratum weights equal to S's, so A matches S on type and difficulty and differs only in detour steps. P: pruned S, detour visits deleted, the pruned action list replayed in the same game, only successful replays kept; coverage of S by stratum reported. Sh: sham-pruned S from exactly P's source items, token-matched to P per item (within 10 percent) by deleting state-neutral non-detour steps and shortening non-detour observations, every detour visit kept; replay-verified. Item tokens measured (E about 140; S about 2x; P about E; Sh equal to P).
- Routes. RET: goal-sentence top-3 (the Measurement A retriever), uncached; retrieved ids, ranks, lengths and detour steps logged per episode. Composition arms (same retriever, same games): M1 = top S item at rank 1 then top-2 E; M2 = top E item at rank 1 then top-2 S. WB: whole bank as a type-agnostic cached prefix. Block design: the 274 games form 8 type-stratified blocks (about 34 games); each (block, seed) gets its own random type-balanced bank from the pool (8s bank draws per WB arm at s seeds); within each seed the S banks are tilted (2 blocks from the bottom detour tercile within type, 4 uniform, 2 from the top) so the bank-mean detour spans the pool's range while the arm mean equals the pool mean; episodes run block by block so one prefix is hot at a time. Rungs: E at 6 and 48 items, S at 6, 24, 48. Fit rule fixed before the run: 48 if a 48-item S prefix plus a 3k-token history reserve fits 16k, else the largest multiple of 6 that fits, for both pools. Token-matched WB E48 vs WB S24 also reported.
- static3-S: 3 fixed type-conditioned S exemplars (S counterpart of Measurement C's static3), cached.
- Arms at Qwen3-32B, each 274 games x 2 seeds = 548 episodes paired on (game, seed) with Measurements A and C: RET S, RET A, RET P, RET Sh, RET M1, RET M2, static3-S, WB E6, WB E48, WB S6, WB S24, WB S48: 12 arms, 6,576 episodes, about 8 h on two GPUs (about 40 min per arm on two replicas). RET E is Measurement A; k0 and the static arms are Measurement C. Conditional: RET S_P (unpruned versions of P's surviving items) if under 80 percent of S survives pruning (+40 min).
- Seed extension for the headline 2x2 (RET E, RET S, WB48 E, WB48 S): after seeds 1-2 the cluster-robust MDE of the interaction [WB48 S - WB48 E] - [RET S - RET E] is computed blind to its sign (rule and arithmetic in Measurement); if at or above 9 net, seeds 3-4 are run on all four cells (2,192 episodes, about 2.7 h), and if still at or above 9, seeds 5-6 (another 2,192; cap). Other arms stay at two seeds (compared on seeds 1-2). Total 6,576 to 10,960 episodes, about 8 to 13.5 h on two GPUs.
- Outcomes: success (primary), steps and step-limit failures (secondary, paired). Mechanism regressions: in RET arms the per-(game, seed) step difference against RET E on the injected items' detour steps (rank-1 and mean of 3); in WB48 S the step difference against WB48 E on the most-similar prefix item's detour steps (by retriever score, per game) and on the bank-mean detour steps (8s tilted values, cluster bootstrap). Exploratory consensus signature: visits to the type's modal wrong receptacle regressed on its share among the bank's items and on whether the most-similar item visits it.
- Cost: prefill tokens and GPU-seconds per episode under prefix caching (8 prefixes per WB arm and seed); cost per success reported for both routes.
- Order: RET S; positive control RET A vs RET S (stop rule); pre-registration (slope MDE, interaction rule); WB48 E and WB48 S, blinded SE, any seed extension; static3-S; S ladder and WB E6; P and Sh; M1 and M2.
Baselines and Ablations:
- k0 and the Measurement C static arms (static3, procedure paragraph, six-procedure instr_all, wrong-type blind1); every retrieval number is reported in the brief's residual form, retrieval minus the best static arm built from the same pool at matched tokens: for E, static3 (k3 - static3 = +17.2 net [+11.9, +22.4]) or WB48 E, whichever is higher; for S, static3-S or WB48 S, whichever is higher.
- RET E (Measurement A) is the clean-item reference.
- A is the positive control, matched to S on type and expert solution length so the contrast varies detour steps only. P is the repair ablation; Sh is its length control (same items, same tokens removed, detours kept), so P vs Sh isolates detour content from token count and P vs E on covered games isolates phrasing.
- M1 and M2 are the composition ablations: same retriever, same games, self item at rank 1 only or at ranks 2-3 only.
- static3-S is the few-fixed-items counterpart of RET S: it tests whether few detoured items inherit detours whether or not they were retrieved.
- WB E at 6 and 48 is the no-noise reference for the S ladder (6, 24, 48); the tilted per-(block, seed) banks give the whole-bank route a within-arm detour-rate dose at fixed item count.
- Token-matched WB E48 vs WB S24 controls for the longer S items.
- Type conditioning: WB prefixes are type-agnostic; static3-S is type-conditioned like static3; RET selects by goal sentence.
- A random-fixed-selection RET S cell was dropped: the goal-sentence retriever cannot see item length, so retriever length bias is not a live confound; retrieved item lengths are still logged. The Qwen3-8B reader replication was dropped because it carried no prediction; its budget funds the seed extension of the headline cells.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (retrieval inherits detours): RET S minus RET E is at or below -8 net and RET S episodes are longer by at least 2 steps on the paired median. Falsified if RET S is within +/-8 of RET E with no step increase. Mixed outcome (success within +/-8, steps up 2 or more) pre-assigned as inheritance absorbed by the step limit: P1 holds on steps only and P2 is read on its step form; arms: RET S vs RET E. P1b: static3-S is at least 8 net below static3. Falsified if static3-S is within +/-8 of static3 while P1 holds (deficit retrieval-specific, not a few-items effect); not read if P1 fails; arms: static3-S vs static3.
- P2 (route x noise interaction, headline): the paired interaction I = [WB48 S - WB48 E] - [RET S - RET E] on success is at least +9 net, the four cells seed-extended by the blinded rule until the pre-registered cluster-robust MDE for I is below 9 (expected at four seeds, cap six). Falsified if I's cluster-bootstrap 95 percent CI lies below +9 and covers zero (equal losses within the MDE), or if WB48 S loses more than RET S (the arxiv:2405.00200 copying outcome). Step form on the same cells: the paired-mean step interaction is at or below -2 steps (MDE about 1.3 steps at 548 pairs, 1.0 at 1,096); falsified if its CI lies above -2; it becomes the headline only if the success MDE is still at or above 9 at the cap. Residual form alongside: the retrieval residual over the best same-pool static arm (+17.2 over static3 on E) shrinks by at least 9 net on S, WB48 S being the static arm that removes it; arms: WB48 E, WB48 S, RET E, RET S.
- P3 (item-count dose on noisy items): WB S rises from 6 to 48 items by at least 9 net while WB E is flat within +/-8 (16 bank draws per cell; cluster bootstrap). Falsified if WB6 S is within 8 net of WB48 S or above it, or if WB E rises by as much; if WB E6 is within 9 net of the 0.87 ceiling the E-flat half is ceiling-bound and the S rise alone carries P3; arms: WB S6, S24, S48 vs WB E6, E48.
- P4 (pruning repairs through detours, not length): RET P is at least 9 net above RET Sh and above RET S (or RET S_P when run). Falsified if RET P is within +/-8 of RET Sh: both at least 8 above RET S = token-count effect; both within +/-8 of RET S = on-policy phrasing effect. Secondary: RET P within +/-8 of RET E on covered games; P above Sh by 9 yet 8 below RET E = residual phrasing deficit; arms: RET P, RET Sh, RET S, RET E.
- P5 (positive control): RET A is at least 8 net below RET S and its episodes are longer by at least 2 steps on the paired median. Falsified if RET A is within +/-8 of RET S with no step increase: retrieved detours then have no leverage and the design stops; arms: RET A vs RET S (stratum-matched, only detour steps differ).
- P6 (mechanism, equivalence bound): in RET arms (RET S and RET A pooled) the paired slope of episode steps on injected-item detour steps is above zero (95 percent paired bootstrap); in WB48 S the slope on the most-similar prefix item's detour steps has a 95 percent CI inside +/-b, b = half the RET slope, and the slope on the bank-mean detour steps is also inside +/-b (cluster bootstrap over tilted bank draws, exploratory half). Tested only if the RET slope is at least twice the pre-registered MDE (about 0.2 steps per item detour step at 548 episodes), else underpowered. Falsified if the WB most-similar slope's CI excludes zero and its point estimate reaches b (copying); arms: WB48 S (per-(block, seed) banks, most-similar item logged), RET S, RET A.
- P7 (retrieval commits to rank 1): conditional on P1 (d at or below -8), RET M1 (self at rank 1) is at least 8 net below RET E, RET M2 (self at ranks 2-3) is within +/-8 of RET E, and M1 - M2 is at or below -8. Falsified if M1 and M2 are within +/-8 of each other (any single detoured item suffices or position is irrelevant), or if M2 is at least 8 below M1 (inheritance grows with detoured-item count; whole-bank robustness would then be a continuation of k, not a route difference); arms: RET M1, RET M2, RET E, RET S.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired cells on 274 games x 2 seeds with identical seeds across arms and with Measurements A and C; +/-8 net floor for a single paired contrast; confirmatory effects must exceed the floor and be at least one third of the Gate-0 retrieval gain (+27 net at k=3 over k0; +17.2 over static3 in Measurement C, CI half-width about 5). The headline interaction is a four-cell contrast whose floor is not the single-contrast floor. Rule, pre-registered before the 2x2 runs: after seeds 1-2 the cluster-robust SE of the per-(game, seed) interaction (clusters = block x seed, 16) is computed blind to the sign of the estimate; MDE = 1.96 x SE; the four cells are extended in pairs of seeds until the MDE is below 9 net, cap six seeds. Arithmetic: the 8-net single-contrast floor implies an interaction floor of about 11 (independent contrasts) to 16 (worst case) at two seeds, 8-11 at four, 6.5-9.2 at six; the observed k3 - static3 half-width (5.3) implies about 7.5 at two seeds, so the expected stop is four seeds. The step form of the interaction uses the paired mean: with an episode-step SD near 8 the per-pair interaction SD is at most about 16, giving an MDE of about 1.3 steps at 548 pairs and 1.0 at 1,096, recomputed from measured SDs before the run; at the six-seed cap the headline transfers to the step form and the success interaction is reported as underpowered. Steps and step-limit failures are paired per (game, seed) and summarised by median differences (single contrasts) or mean differences (the interaction) with paired or cluster bootstrap intervals. Whole-bank cells average over 8 bank draws per seed; (block x seed) is the cluster for the bank-mean regressor and for a cluster bootstrap of every WB cell and of every contrast containing one. The slope MDE for P6 is computed from the measured episode-step SD (Measurement A) and item detour-step SD before the run and pre-registered together with the equivalence bound b. Per-type results pooled over the three procedure-heavy types (clean, heat, cool) and declared exploratory. Positive control before any null: RET A must be at least 8 net below RET S. Success ceiling (0.87 at k=7) limits headroom, so steps and step-limit failures are pre-registered secondary outcomes on which the imitation claim can still be tested. P's coverage of S by stratum is reported and triggers the RET S_P arm below 80 percent; Sh's achieved token match to P is reported per item. Retrieved item ids, ranks, lengths and detour steps are logged per episode. Cost measured as GPU-seconds per episode and prefill tokens under prefix caching. Pre-registration after the positive control and before the 2x2 cells run.

Risk Factors and Limitations:
- Self-pool items may be too long for 48 to fit in 16k; the fit rule (largest multiple of 6 that fits, used for both pools) is fixed before the run and the token-matched cell covers the length confound.
- The agent may ignore detours in retrieved items, giving a null on P1; the difficulty-matched high-detour positive control is the stop rule, and the manipulation is built in rather than observed.
- The headline interaction needs more episodes than a single contrast; the blinded extension uses only the SD of the interaction from seeds 1-2 (an internal pilot), so the same episodes inform both the sample size and the estimate; the cap, the margin and the transfer-to-steps rule are fixed before the 2x2 runs, and the extra cost (up to 4,384 episodes, about 5.4 h) is funded by dropping the Qwen3-8B replication, so no reader generalisation is claimed.
- Rule-based pruning can break trajectories; replay validation keeps only successful pruned items, which can bias P toward easier games; Sh is built from the same items so P vs Sh is unbiased, coverage is reported, and RET S_P is run if coverage falls below 80 percent.
- Sh matches tokens, not format: shortening observations changes the item's look; if that alone moves success it shows as RET Sh differing from RET S at equal detours and is reported.
- Banks drawn per (block, seed) make a WB cell's seed-to-seed difference a bank effect plus a sampling effect; this is intended (16 to 48 clusters instead of 8) and the cluster bootstrap absorbs it, but the bank-mean regressor stays the exploratory half of P6. More prefixes per WB arm lower the cache hit rate; cost is logged as run, not assumed.
- M1 and M2 conflate similarity rank with prompt position and one versus two self items; a reversed-order variant is not run.
- The success ceiling near 0.87 limits success-rate headroom; steps and step-limit failures carry part of the claim and are pre-registered as secondary outcomes, and the step form of P2 is the fallback headline.
- If the whole-bank route copies the most similar item (the 2405.00200 outcome), P2 and P6 are falsified; that result would still be informative for the axis and is reported as such.
- P7 is moot if P1 is null; P6 is reported as underpowered rather than confirmed if the RET slope is below twice the MDE.
Addresses gap: G20 (primary): whether long-context scaling conclusions (that long-context ICL keys on the most similar example) transfer to trajectory banks with on-policy noise; also G19 (whole-bank vs retrieval past saturation, here under a manipulated item-noise rate).
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: 'the self pool contains the agent's own detours and is the on-policy counterpart of a curated playbook' names the pool; this idea claims that the read route decides whether detours are inherited, with the detour rate built at several levels (expert, self, difficulty-matched high-detour, tilted whole-bank draws) and pruning against a sham-prune as the repair, which the brief does not claim. Nearest digest card: arxiv:2605.24117 observes that larger libraries add episode-specific drift and clutter under an unspecified selection; this idea claims drift transfers through the rank-1 retrieved item (tested by forced composition) and is averaged out by whole-bank reading, and tests the most-similar-copying alternative directly with a pre-registered slope bound. Nearest archived idea: abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) concerns compiled abstraction losing repairs; here no abstraction is applied and the claim is about raw items under two read routes; first_item_additive_rest_substitutive concerns k on clean items, not item noise.

- P2 (headline, flagged unresolvable): the four-cell interaction now has its own pre-registered MDE (1.96 x cluster-robust SE, clusters = block x seed) computed blind to the sign after seeds 1-2, and the four cells RET E, RET S, WB48 E, WB48 S are extended in pairs of seeds until the MDE is below the +9 margin (arithmetic stated: about 11-16 net at two seeds, 8-11 at four, 6.5-9.2 at six; cap six); the falsifier is restated against that MDE. A pre-registered step form of the same interaction (at or below -2 steps, MDE about 1.3 steps at 548 from the measured step SD) is the second channel and becomes the headline only if the cap is reached. The +9 margin and the copying falsifier are unchanged.
- Bank draws are now per (block, seed) rather than per block, so every WB cell has 8 draws per seed (16 to 48 clusters instead of 8); the S tilt is applied within each seed; the cluster bootstrap and P6's bank-mean regressor use these clusters.
- P1: the mixed outcome (success null, steps up by 2) is pre-assigned; P1b is not read if P1 fails. P3: ceiling guard for the WB-E-flat half and the cluster count stated. P6: cluster count updated. P4, P5, P7 unchanged.
- Budget: the Qwen3-8B replication (no prediction) is dropped to fund the seed extension; all other arms stay at two seeds; total 6,576 to 10,960 episodes, about 8 to 13.5 h on two GPUs, plus the conditional RET S_P.
